technical_debt.title: Validacion E2E con modelo real
technical_debt.detail: La cadena completa (Settings -> adapter -> gateway -> proveedor -> usage -> validacion Pydantic) NO se ha ejecutado contra un proveedor real: no hay credenciales en el entorno. El mecanismo esta implementado y la prueba existe (tests/test_model_gateway_real.py), pero se SALTA en lugar de pasar en falso.
technical_debt.how_to_close: Definir AI_SWE_MODEL_API_KEY, AI_SWE_MODEL_NAME y AI_SWE_MODEL_PROVIDER en .env y ejecutar: AI_SWE_RUN_REAL_PROVIDER_TESTS=1 python -m pytest tests/test_model_gateway_real.py -m real_provider
technical_debt.decision: APLAZADA por decision del Arquitecto (2026-10-07): se sigue trabajando con FakeModelAdapter y el fallback determinista para mantener la suite rapida y offline.
technical_debt.risk_if_unclosed: Un fallo de integracion real (forma de la respuesta, cabeceras, formato de usage del proveedor) no se detectaria hasta el primer uso con un proveedor de verdad.

f3_caveats: Only `interpret`, `plan` and `coder` are connected to the gateway; every other node stays deterministic
The real-provider test is opt-in and was NOT executed: no credentials in the environment (see technical_debt TD-01)
AI_SWE_MODEL_PRICING is empty in the repository, so cost is None (unknown), never 0
The pricing table has a loading mechanism but no tariff is asserted as current
No authentication yet (open finding from the external audit)
f4_caveats: RunPlan is the contract that bounds the plan: DFS cycle detection, unique ids, existing dependencies, <=32 subtasks, agent != supervisor, non-empty allowed_tools
max_review_cycles is clamped to the run budget when the model asks for more; the clamp is declared in the rationale
Topology edges are static: a plan -circular or gigantic- can never introduce a loop in the execution
The deterministic fallback is declared with a recoverable MODEL_FALLBACK error, never silent
f5_caveats: Execution is now subtask-by-subtask via plan_index; the router reads the index and sends to the next agent
Evidence accumulates immutably: each researcher execution concatenates findings to the previous ones
All executor nodes (researcher, coder) advance plan_index by 1; the router only compares, never calculates
The plan is consumed sequentially; dependencies (depends_on) are NOT yet respected before execution (F6)
When the plan is exhausted, execution goes to finalize regardless of intent (the plan is the source of truth)
f6_caveats: The model generates a CodeProposal (path, operation, new_content, rationale); it never generates a CodeChange
The system -not the model- derives the unified diff, the added/removed line counts and every sha256: a model cannot know the hash of a file it has not written
FileOperation (create/modify/delete) exists because a deleted file with added=0/removed=N is indistinguishable from a modified one
The unified diff is line-level and has no old content: `create` treats the previous file as empty, `delete` as fully removed. F7 (sandbox) is what will hold both versions
Scope limits (max_files_changed, max_lines_changed) are enforced by trimming and the trim is declared with a SCOPE_TRIMMED error, never silent
The fallback is a controlled EMPTY change plus a recoverable MODEL_FALLBACK error: no invented patch, ever
The Coder consumes budget and writes NOTHING to disk; applying the patch is F7
ProjectRequirements does not exist (NOT_IMPLEMENTED per the F2 audit): the Coder works from TaskInterpretation, Evidence and the current Subtask
f7_caveats: The sandbox is a real `git worktree` per run, created detached at HEAD under workspace_root (var/workspaces/<run_id>), which is gitignored: the original repo never sees the changes
The sandbox requires a real git repository and a commit: `git worktree add` cannot work without a HEAD

Confinement is four barriers per write: normalize_rel_path (syntax) + path_within_scope (declared scope) + Policy Engine decide() (role/subtask/protection/budget) + the physical check that the resolved path stays inside the sandbox root
A blocked path is a DENIAL, not a fault: it is recorded in `denegados` and the rest of the change still applies - one malicious file does not abort a legitimate change

The unified diff is now real (difflib, old vs new content) when the sandbox supplies the previous content; without it the diff still degrades to the F6 whole-file form and the `/dev/null` header declares it
`git diff HEAD` does not see untracked files: the sandbox runs `git add -N` first, otherwise a `create` would report an empty diff
The Coder CANNOT delete: `delete_file` is Supervisor-only and approval-gated, so a proposed `delete` is denied by policy and the file survives in the sandbox
The sandbox is NOT yet wired into the graph: F7 provides the mechanism (create/apply/teardown) plus tests; promotion of changes to the user repo is not implemented

The fourth barrier (physical root check) is covered by a test that INJECTS the resolution for the destination path, because the canonical attack vector - a symlink inside the worktree pointing outside - cannot be constructed on this Windows machine: `os.symlink` for directories creates a link that neither `Path.resolve()` nor `os.path.realpath()` follows, so resolution never leaves the root and the barrier has nothing to judge. `test_la_plataforma_no_permite_construir_el_vector_de_enlace` asserts the observable platform behaviour instead of skipping and pretending coverage

The teardown has redundant safety nets on this git (2.55.0): `git worktree remove --force` with an absolute path already removes the tree AND the `.git/worktrees/` entry, both for a present tree and for a ghost whose directory vanished. `prune` and the trailing `rmtree` are therefore defence-in-depth whose observable effect is nil today; they are kept, but credited to nobody

`git worktree add <path> HEAD` already detaches on its own (HEAD is a commit-ish), so `--detach` is redundant whenever HEAD is passed; the dangerous form is `git worktree add <path>` with no commit-ish, which creates a branch named after the directory and registers it in the user's repo

A mutation is only valid if it describes a failure the code can actually commit: three F7 mutations targeted redundant lines and passed green with and without them. They were rewritten to attack observable behaviour, not counted as caught

A pytest timeout used to be recorded as `cazada`, which is a false positive: no test ran and failed. `_run_pytest` now returns None on timeout and the verdict is NO CONCLUYENTE; LIMITE_PYTEST was raised 300 -> 600 s because the mutated suite is slower than the base one
rules: Keep LangGraph
Keep RunState typed
LLM proposes; deterministic code validates
No direct Coder writes to main workspace
No shell=True with LLM-generated commands
No MCP/Graphify before M2 E2E
No exposure beyond localhost before auth
New Budget fields enter with defaults; only removal/rename bumps schema version
A passing test proves nothing until a mutation makes it fail
No agent imports a provider SDK; all go through ModelGateway
Only models/providers/ may know about a concrete provider
The standard suite must pass without internet, credentials or an external provider
F3: only `interpret` may talk to the gateway; the deterministic classifier is the permanent fallback
F3: a model failure degrades to the fallback and leaves a recoverable error; it is never silent
F3: the interpreter's scope comes from the user, never from the model
F4: the plan is data, not topology; edges are written by hand and never generated from the plan
F4: the plan always passes through the RunPlan contract; model_construct is never used
F4: a model failure degrades to a deterministic plan and leaves a recoverable error; it is never silent
F4: a plan can never promise more review cycles than the run budget allows
F5: plan_index is the single source of truth for progress; it lives in RunState, not duplicated elsewhere
F5: the executor node advances plan_index; the router only reads it, never calculates
F5: evidence accumulates immutably; no executor overwrites the output of a previous subtask
F5: when the plan is exhausted, execution finalizes; the static M1 route does not apply
F6: the model proposes content; the code derives diff, line counts and hashes -the model never supplies a hash
F6: CodeProposal is what the model generates and CodeChange is what the system derives; they are different contracts on purpose
F6: a `delete` carries no new_content and a `create`/`modify` requires it; the contract rejects the incoherence at the boundary
F6: exceeding Scope limits trims and declares (SCOPE_TRIMMED); it never truncates silently and never discards the whole change
F6: a model failure degrades to a controlled EMPTY change with a recoverable error; inventing a patch is forbidden
F6: the Coder never writes to disk; it only fills RunState.outputs.coder_output (F7 applies the patch)
F6: a model failure must APPEND its error to the existing ones; it must never overwrite the errors of earlier phases
F7: the Coder proposes, the sandbox applies; the Coder never writes to disk and never to the user repo
F7: every write inside the sandbox passes confinement before any effect - never once at the start, always per file
F7: confinement is four barriers (syntax, declared scope, policy, physical root check); any one of them denies
F7: a denied path is recorded and skipped; the remaining legitimate files of the same change still apply
F7: the sandbox is a git worktree, created detached, under a gitignored workspace root, and teardown removes AND prunes
F7: the diff is a real unified diff when the previous content is available; without it, the degradation is declared, never silent
F7: the Coder cannot delete files; destructiveness requires approval and the Supervisor role

F7: the fourth barrier is tested by injecting the resolution outcome, not by planting a symlink: the platform cannot produce a symlink that resolution follows, and a link the system does not resolve proves nothing about the code that judges the resolved path
F7: a mutation must describe a failure the code can commit; a mutation over a redundant line passes green with and without it and verifies nothing
F7: a pytest timeout is NOT a caught mutation -no test failed-; it is reported as non-conclusive, never silently counted as caught
F7: redundancy in the teardown is proven against the filesystem, not assumed; `prune`/`rmtree` are kept as defence in depth but are not credited as the mechanism
F8: a test target is not a command; the id is resolved through a closed in-code table and passed to subprocess as an argument list with shell=False
F8: tests run inside the sandbox worktree, never in the user repo, and the child's PYTHONPATH points at the sandbox src/ so the evidence describes the code that will be approved
F8: a red test is evidence for the Reviewer, not a system error; a timeout is evidence of a hang, not an exception
F8: a sandbox failure becomes a typed RunError and the run ends in needs_human, never a LangGraph traceback
F8: a branch that never executes looks covered; the `fallos` branch was unreachable because a raw OSError escaped before reaching it -writing the test found a defect, not just a blind spot
F8: conditional edges do not appear in get_graph().edges; assert topology on the uncompiled StateGraph (nodes + branches) and by exercising the routers

next_step_proposed.why: It is the last unmet item of the M2 Definition of Done (item 9). The reviewer is still deterministic; with F8 it now has real test evidence to judge, but it does not yet reason about requirements + change + tests.
next_step_proposed.scope: Make the Reviewer model-driven: it must weigh the original requirements, the applied change and the real TestRun evidence, and return a typed ReviewVerdict. Keep the deterministic verdict as the fallback when no model is connected, and keep the bounded review cycle (REQUEST_CHANGES -> coder while review_cycles_used < max_review_cycles).
